name: Primocane vs floricane
summary: On raspberry and blackberry, first-year canes (primocanes) and second-year canes (floricanes) fruit on different schedules — the distinction that drives pruning, trellis, and harvest timing. Blueberry does not use this two-year cane pattern.
what_is_it: A primocane is a first-year cane. A floricane is that same cane in its second year. Floricane-fruiting (summer-bearing) types flower and fruit on second-year wood, then that cane is removed. Primocane-fruiting (fall-bearing / everbearing) types can fruit on first-year canes, which changes pruning and can enable a later harvest or, in some systems, two crops. Dual-cropping types can do both. This is caneberry biology; highbush blueberry shoots do not follow a primocane/floricane fruiting calendar.
why_it_matters: The habit determines when fruit is picked, how the plant is pruned, what trellis is used, and which climates are commercially realistic. Primocane-fruiting blackberry (for example University of Arkansas Prime-Ark series) is often discussed as expanding where blackberry can be grown because first-year fruiting reduces winter-cane survival risk. A news item about a 'primocane blackberry' is unintelligible without this distinction.
how_evaluated: Nurseries and variety descriptions state the habit as a category (primocane, floricane, or both). In the field it is observed from which canes carry flowers and fruit, and from the pruning system in use. It is not a Brix reading or a firmness instrument value.
what_affects_it: Genetics set the habit. Climate, winter injury, tipping, and whether a grower manages for a single fall crop or also a summer floricane crop change how the habit is used commercially. The same cultivar can be managed differently by region.
how_to_interpret: Do not treat 'primocane' as a quality grade or a claim that fruit is sweeter. It names cane-year fruiting biology. Blueberry 'everbearing' marketing is a different plant. When intelligence names a primocane raspberry or blackberry, look for the crop, the habit, and the geography before generalizing to other berries or to commercial success.

berry_notes.note: Raspberry pruning, trellis, and harvest timing are this distinction. Biennial-cane (floricane) types and primocane-fruiting types are managed as different systems.
Primocane-fruiting blackberry (including University of Arkansas Prime-Ark series) is why 'first-year fruiting' shows up in commercial expansion talk. Trailing vs erect still changes the trellis.
